Arctic indigenous peoples. The Inuit hunted seals and whales via kayaks and harpoons across Arctic coastlines from Alaska to Greenland. The Sami herded reindeer across Northern Scandinavia, domesticating the only Arctic reindeer. Siberian peoples including Yakuts and Chukchi maintained diverse hunting and herding economies. European contact from the sixteenth century onward brought disease epidemics, forced assimilation in residential schools, and land dispossession. Contemporary issues include climate change disrupting hunting patterns and sovereignty disputes over Arctic resources.
